newsitem.title: ITALY: Sleep in your designer suit, Dolce & Gabbana style.
newsitem.headline: Sleep in your designer suit, Dolce & Gabbana style.

text.p: Italian design duo Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana showed sleeping in a suit could put a man at the forefront of fashion when they opened the Milan menswear shows with a new, crumpled look on Sunday.

Dolce and Gabbana, illustrating their ready-to-wear collection before the runway presentation, said delicate suit fabrics and linens had been washed to give a permanent wrinkle to jackets, pants and jerseys.
Crumpled hand-stitched suit jackets, buttoned high to small collars, contrasted with narrow-waisted trousers which bagged down the thigh and flopped wide in a turn-up over the shoe.
The twosome, demonstrating the clothes in a reception room where leopardskin print covered the walls from floor to ceiling, said proportion was also key to a fresh male profile.
The slender but unrestrictive jackets contrasted with the wide-legged pants for a tailored but comfortable effect which, Gabbana added, "is not Charlie Chaplin."
They said quality was a high priority in the new "lived-in" look, with emphasis on Neapolitan tailoring and natural fibres.

They had split the collection in two, leaving everyday wear off the runway but parading more avant-garde pieces in an attempt to displace a minimalist trend, which they said had left many labels looking the same.

"It's very important at the moment to give people a new dream," Gabbana told Reuters backstage later. "I think men want to wear fashion again - I don't know if they want the size or the leather but I feel this and I'm presenting this."
"This is a test for Dolce & Gabbana," Dolce said.

Innovations included a reversible blue and beige fine-knit jersey which was in fact two pullovers joined at the bottom hem and cuff with a band of the interior colour flashing out at the base. Sleeves were oversized and pullovers had a twist to the knit as if they were being pulled round the body to one side.
"The idea in all the collection is twist and movement," Gabbana said.
Another detail was the "one-and-a-half" breasted suit jacket with buttons fastening deeper into the front panel than a single breasted jacket but not as far over as a double.

Casual pants stopped short at the ankle and were narrow but not skin-tight with nickel zippers up the ankle or inside leg, while leather and suede jackets were cut leaving raw edges and external seams.
Colours included olive green on military-style jackets, red knits contrasted with camel trousers and blacks and dark blues.
Shoes had no laces in the holes but fastened with leather straps and velcro or elastic over the bridge, while casual footwear resembled thin-soled pumps worn by Olympic gymnasts.
The shows run until Thursday with luxury design house Gucci unveiling its collection on Tuesday, Prada on Wednesday and top designer Giorgio Armani closing the season on Thursday.
